merger_name: Veritas Capital Fund Management – BGIS Group

anzsic_codes.name: Engineering Design and Engineering Consulting Services

merger_description:
Funds managed (directly or indirectly) by Veritas Capital Fund Management, L.L.C. (**Veritas**), through Naples Bidco Limited, propose to indirectly acquire control of BIFM Jersey Topco Limited and its subsidiaries (the **BGIS Group**) (the **Acquisition**).

Veritas is a private equity fund adviser incorporated and based in the United States. It invests in companies that provide products, software, and services, primarily technology and technology-enabled solutions, to government and commercial customers worldwide.

The BGIS Group is headquartered in Ontario, Canada, and is a global provider of integrated facilities management services, offering end-to-end outsourced facility management, engineering, and advisory services to commercial and government customers. This involves managing the day-to-day operations, maintenance, and sustainability of large-scale built environments, including complex infrastructure, such as data centres, hospitals and high-security government facilities.

events.title: Notification waiver determination published

determination_table_content.details:
In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver application and
had regard to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition
and Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information provided by the applicant, the ACCC
considers that the Acquisition is unlikely to give rise to any material
lessening of competition given:
a. there is limited horizontal overlap between Veritas (and its
portfolio companies, as well as Trinity Consultants) and the
BGIS Group in the supply of facility management,
engineering and advisory services in Australia
b. there are alternative suppliers of facility management,
engineering and advisory services in Australia.
In these circumstances, the ACCC does not consider it necessary to
reach a concluded view on the likelihood of the notification
thresholds being met.
Given that material competition concerns are unlikely to arise, the
ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s guidance on notification
waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
